tools.name: compose_kit
tools.description: **THE BUILD KIT — start here for a new product or feature.** Takes a plain-English brief and returns a generation instruction with AsciiKit's design-intelligence pack bound in, so you produce the three connected documents the user hands to their AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, v0, Lovable) to build the right thing instead of generic AI slop: journey.md (screens + flow + psychological moments), prd.md (requirements with acceptance criteria), and DESIGN.md (a governed design system + anti-slop "don'ts"). After calling this, follow the returned instruction — use render_component()/compose_wireframe() for any wireframes. Use this when the user describes something they want to build and needs build-ready docs, not just a single wireframe.

brief.description: Plain-English description of what the user is building — what it is, who it is for, and the core thing a user needs to do.

product_name.description: Optional product or feature name. Derived from the brief if omitted.

domain.description: Optional domain hint like fintech, health, social, education.

constraints.description: Optional natural-language design constraints, e.g. "no dark patterns", "accessible", "calm and trustworthy".

tools.name: get_visual_language
tools.description: Returns a complete reference guide of all 57 available UI components you can build with render_component(). Use this to see what components are available (buttons, form fields, cards, charts, navigation, metrics, etc.) and their required parameters. This is a REFERENCE ONLY - you still must call render_component() for each element. The visual language includes examples, parameter requirements, and visual previews of each component type.

tools.name: get_design_intelligence
tools.description: Returns comprehensive design intelligence based on context - psychology, IA, cognitive science, emotional design, conversion tactics, and accessibility

domain.description: Domain like fintech, health, social, education

screen_type.description: Screen type like dashboard, onboarding, checkout, settings

user_goal.description: What the user is trying to accomplish

user_segment.description: Target user group like seniors, experts, beginners

emotional_target.description: Target emotion like trust, excitement, calm

culture.description: Cultural market context like us, japan, india, germany, brazil, china, uk, middle_east. Activates culture-specific trust mechanics and IA patterns.

include.description: Specific intelligence types to include (psychology, information_architecture, cognitive, emotional, conversion, accessibility)

oneOf.description: Natural language constraints like "no dark patterns", "make it accessible", "family-friendly"

constraints.description: Design constraints (natural language string or structured array)

tools.name: compose_wireframe
tools.description: **STEP 2: ASSEMBLE THE FINAL WIREFRAME** - Takes an array of WireframeComponent objects (from render_component() calls in Step 1) and composes them into a complete 38-character-wide ASCII wireframe. **CRITICAL WORKFLOW:** You MUST call render_component() first for each UI element, THEN pass the array here. DO NOT create component JSON manually. DO NOT pass raw string arrays. Example: const components = [headerComponent, emailFieldComponent, passwordFieldComponent, buttonComponent]; compose_wireframe({components, screenType: "mobile"}). The engine automatically applies psychological design patterns (trust signals, thumb zones, accessibility spacing) based on intelligence context. Returns the rendered wireframe ready to show the user.

components.description: Array of WireframeComponent objects returned from render_component() calls. Each component has: type (header|navigation|content|form|list|card|footer|modal|empty), content (array of strings), and height (number). IMPORTANT: Get these from render_component() tool, do NOT manually create them.

flowPosition.description: Optional flow position context for multi-step flows

tools.name: validate_wireframe
tools.description: Validates that every line of a wireframe is exactly 38 characters wide

tools.name: render_components
tools.description: **BATCH RENDER** - Render multiple UI components in a single call. Pass an array of {componentType, params} objects and get back all rendered WireframeComponent objects ready for compose_wireframe(). Much faster than calling render_component() individually for each element. Example: render_components({components: [{componentType: "header", params: {title: "Login"}}, {componentType: "form_field_with_label", params: {label: "Email"}}, {componentType: "primary_button", params: {label: "Sign In"}}]})

components.description: Array of components to render, each with componentType and params

componentType.description: Component type (see render_component for full list)

tools.name: render_component
tools.description: **STEP 1: BUILD INDIVIDUAL UI ELEMENTS** - Call this tool ONCE for EACH UI element in your wireframe (button, text field, card, list item, etc.). Each call returns a properly formatted WireframeComponent object. **YOU MUST USE THIS TOOL - DO NOT manually create component JSON.** Example: To build a login screen, call render_component() 5 times: 1) render_component('header', {title: 'Login'}) 2) render_component('form_field_with_label', {label: 'Email', value: ''}) 3) render_component('form_field_with_label', {label: 'Password', value: ''}) 4) render_component('primary_button', {label: 'Sign In'}) 5) render_component('helper_text', {text: 'Forgot password?'}). THEN collect all 5 components into an array and pass to compose_wireframe() in Step 2. Available components: buttons, form fields, cards, metrics, lists, navigation, charts, progress bars, etc. See get_visual_language() for full list.

componentType.description: Which atom renderer to use. See get_visual_language() for full list with examples and parameter requirements.

params.description: Parameters for the atom renderer. Varies by component type. Common params: label, value, text, title, options. See documentation for each component type.
